PullRequest.Title: Cache and coalesce marketplace protected resource discovery
PullRequest.Body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.

-->

Follow-up to [microsoft/vscode#325804](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/325804), for [microsoft/vscode#325412](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/325412).

Cache successful RFC 9728 discovery for five minutes after completion and coalesce concurrent lookups. The cache holds only the current service URL, including its path; failed, missing, and unusable metadata remain immediately retryable.

Interactive consent uses the same bounded cache and ignores obsolete discovery or silent-session results after URL changes, expiration, metadata replacement, or provider disposal. Replacement providers start with an empty cache. Token acquisition still runs on every account lookup; token lifetimes, fallback behavior, refresh, 403 mapping, and GitHub discovery are unchanged.

## Validation

- `node build\npm\electronTypes.ts` - passed.
- `npm run typecheck-client` - passed.
- `npm run transpile-client` - passed.
- `npm run valid-layers-check` - passed.
- `npm run precommit` - passed for both changed files.
- `$env:VSCODE_SKIP_PRELAUNCH = '1'; .\scripts\test.bat --run src\vs\workbench\services\extensionManagement\test\electron-browser\extensionGalleryAccountService.test.ts --run src\vs\workbench\services\extensionManagement\test\electron-browser\extensionGalleryManifestService.test.ts --reporter dot` - passed, 80 tests.

The new deterministic regressions cover repeated and concurrent reuse, exact expiration without sliding on reads, failed-discovery retries, full-URL invalidation, provider replacement, and stale discovery/consent races.

No live private marketplace or interactive identity-provider validation was performed.

RegressionFixes.Mechanism: Each private-marketplace account revalidation repeated RFC 9728 protected-resource metadata discovery, including sequential authentication-session events and concurrent resolutions, producing redundant network requests on the manifest/account critical path.
RegressionFixes.Symptom: Repeated or concurrent marketplace account revalidation incurred avoidable network latency and request load before the private marketplace manifest could be refreshed.
RegressionFixes.FixedBehavior: Successful protected-resource metadata is reused for the same full service URL for five minutes, and concurrent cold lookups share one discovery promise. Failures remain retryable, URL/provider changes invalidate the cache, and resource-scoped token acquisition still executes on every account lookup.
RegressionFixes.Evidence: Base line 208 invoked discoverProtectedResource(serviceIndexUrl) for every eligible Microsoft account resolution. WorkbenchExtensionGalleryManifestService.handleMarketplaceAccountAccess calls getAccount on initial private-marketplace bootstrap and again for each Microsoft onDidChangeSessions event; fetchResourceMetadata crosses IRequestService and can issue one well-known GET for root URLs or a path-appended GET plus root fallback for path URLs. The added successful-value check and in-flight request reuse remove repeated discovery while preserving per-resolution token acquisition. Added tests prove sequential resolutions perform one metadata request and three concurrent resolutions coalesce to one.

Scenarios.CriticalPath: WorkbenchExtensionGalleryManifestService construction eagerly starts manifest resolution. MicrosoftGalleryAccountProvider.getAccount must obtain the sign-in session, discover protected-resource metadata on a cold cache, obtain the resource-scoped session, and then fetch/parse the marketplace manifest before the marketplace becomes available. On a warm metadata cache, discovery is removed from this critical path; token and manifest operations remain required.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Query Microsoft authentication sessions for the configured sign-in scopes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One call per account resolution, independent of metadata cache state.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same sign-in session lookup ran for every resolution.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must complete before eligibility and marketplace access can be resolved.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch RFC 9728 protected-resource metadata through IRequestService.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Cold successful root URL: one GET; a service URL with a path can require path-appended discovery and one root fallback. Warm successful cache: zero for five minutes. Concurrent cold resolutions for one URL share this cardinality.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Every eligible account resolution performed discovery, with concurrent resolutions issuing independent requests.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cold discovery blocks resource-session selection; warm discovery is bypassed.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Query the Microsoft authentication provider for a resource-scoped session.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One call per eligible resolution when usable protected-resource metadata exists; not cached by this diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same resource-session query ran after every successful metadata discovery.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks selection of the bearer used for the marketplace manifest.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch and parse the configured marketplace service index.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One request per non-superseded eligible resolution.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must complete before the private marketplace manifest becomes available.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The prior cost scaled with eligible account-resolution count and concurrent authentication events. After the diff, metadata network cost scales with distinct sequential service URLs and five-minute cache windows; production normally has one configured service URL.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The steps within one resolution are awaited serially. Concurrent account resolutions share one metadata discovery promise for the current exact service URL; the manifest service separately cancels superseded resolutions but does not add concurrency in this diff.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: One positive entry is keyed by the exact service URL, including path. Its five-minute TTL starts after successful discovery and does not slide on reads. In-flight cold requests are coalesced. Missing, invalid, failed, or unusable metadata is not negatively cached and is retried. URL changes and provider replacement create empty cache state.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: direct call flow and deterministic tests establish both the old per-resolution boundary and the new one-request cache/coalescing behavior.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Authentication event frequency and real metadata endpoint latency vary by provider and deployment, but the removed network-call multiplicity and startup critical-path reachability are direct.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression. The diff removes repeated network discovery and concurrent fan-out without adding work to warm bootstrap.

Scenarios.Scenario: Microsoft authentication-session change and marketplace revalidation
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each Microsoft onDidChangeSessions event fires the account-change event, which starts handleMarketplaceAccountAccess. Sign-in session lookup, resource token lookup, and manifest fetch remain on the revalidation path; protected-resource discovery is now off-path on a valid warm cache.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve sign-in and resource-scoped Microsoft authentication sessions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Up to two provider calls per eligible event; unchanged and not coalesced by this PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Both must complete before the event can publish a refreshed marketplace authorization.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Zero on warm success; one logical discovery per URL/TTL across concurrent events, potentially two GETs only when path discovery falls back to root.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: One logical discovery per eligible event, with no sequential cache or concurrent coalescing.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks only cold/expired revalidation; warm events skip it.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Refetch marketplace manifest for the resolved account.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one active request per event, with superseded requests cancellation-signaled; unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required for the latest account catalog to be published.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Event count and event burst width determine auth-provider and manifest work; metadata discovery is reduced from event count to URL/TTL-window count after coalescing.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Rapid events can overlap at the manifest-service level; beginResolution cancels older manifest resolutions. The added cache coalesces only metadata discovery globally for the current URL, while sign-in/resource-session lookups still execute per resolution as before.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Concurrent events for the same URL share an in-flight metadata promise, and subsequent events reuse a successful value until fixed expiration. Failed discovery is immediately retryable, so a sustained endpoint failure can still produce one attempt per sequential event, matching prior retry semantics rather than adding work.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: provider event wiring, manifest handler, and cache request identity checks are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Real session-event burst rates are deployment-dependent; tests and event wiring prove this path exists.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression. The changed mechanism bounds repeated metadata I/O while preserving unchanged per-event token and manifest refresh work.

Scenarios.Scenario: Interactive Microsoft marketplace sign-in and protected-resource consent
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The user-triggered flow creates the sign-in session, obtains metadata from the captured current cache, checks silently for an existing resource-scoped session, and only then may create an interactive resource-scoped session. Metadata discovery is off-path when the cache is warm, but a missing or expired cache is refreshed before consent.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Enumerate accounts and create the selected Microsoft sign-in session.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One account enumeration and one sign-in session creation per completed user choice.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: User interaction and provider session creation are the main sign-in critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch current protected-resource metadata when absent or expired.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Zero warm; one coalesced logical discovery cold/expired, with optional root fallback for path URLs.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: After any prior successful discovery, sign-in reused metadata indefinitely; if none existed but a service URL was known, it performed discovery.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cold/expired discovery is awaited before resource consent. The diff can refresh after five minutes where the old indefinite value avoided this request, an intentional freshness bound; cardinality is one and coalesced.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Check for and, if needed, create a resource-scoped Microsoft session.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One silent check and at most one interactive creation per consent flow.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same operations, using the last indefinitely retained metadata.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The silent check and optional consent must finish before signIn resolves.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Cost scales with user sign-in attempts and cache expiration windows, not marketplace catalog size. Concurrent attempts share discovery but retain their own authentication-provider operations.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Operations in one consent flow are serial. Any concurrent account lookup for the same URL shares metadata discovery. Cache identity, expiration, provider disposal, or URL replacement aborts stale consent rather than launching additional resource-session creation.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Consent captures the current one-entry URL cache. It uses a successful warm value, joins an in-flight request, or refreshes an expired value. Before prompting for resource consent it rechecks provider ownership, cache identity/value, and expiration. Failures are not cached and simply skip resource consent for that attempt.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the serial awaits and stale-result guards are explicit and covered by race/expiration tests.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Endpoint latency after expiration varies, but this is a bounded single discovery required to avoid using stale authorization metadata; there is no evidenced harmful burst or unbounded delay introduced by the cache design itself.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The bounded refresh can add one network round trip to an expired interactive flow, but it is required by the stated freshness semantics, coalesced, and does not create scaling fan-out.

Scenarios.Scenario: Service URL change and provider replacement
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A resolution for a different full service URL replaces the one-entry cache; provider replacement starts with a new empty provider cache. The next eligible lookup performs fresh metadata discovery before token acquisition.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Discover metadata separately for the new service URL while an obsolete URL request may still be in flight.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One logical discovery for each effective URL transition; at most the obsolete request plus the current request overlap in the traced transition. Returning to a previous URL creates another cold request because this is deliberately a one-entry cache.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Every resolution discovered afresh, so URL transitions also issued new requests and old requests could remain in flight.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Only the current URL discovery can advance the new resolution; obsolete completion is ignored.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Network cost scales with URL transitions rather than historical distinct URLs; realistic production configuration has one active URL and configuration changes require restart.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Old in-flight discovery is not canceled at the transport layer, but its result is rejected by cache identity checks. A new URL may therefore overlap with one obsolete request; repeated same-URL callers still coalesce on the current cache.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The cache key is the complete service URL string. There is no multi-URL retention, preventing unbounded key growth. Provider disposal/replacement invalidates ownership, and replacement providers never inherit metadata.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: one-entry replacement and stale-object identity checks are direct.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Tests synthesize rapid URL alternation; normal product flow rarely changes URL without restart.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression. The design bounds memory to one entry and prevents obsolete requests from repopulating current state; lack of transport cancellation is pre-existing and does not increase request cardinality.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over the full two-file diff. No diff-introduced performance issue met the reporting bar. The production change is a bounded one-entry positive cache with fixed TTL and in-flight coalescing that removes repeated RFC 9728 network discovery; failures remain retryable and ownership/URL transitions are guarded. Recorded the concrete repeated-network regression fix against introducing commit d71149f1290a26993dda238eb699f2d3aa4c254c.
